title: Mercy at every door
hook: every surah but one opens with mercy, and mercy is the first name after Allah

segments.voice: Yesterday: justice, and your line, stand for justice. The book holds justice level, and then it does something else at every single door.

Flip through a printed Qur'an. Every few pages a decorated panel announces a new surah's name, and right under it, one line, the same line, again and again. Bismillahi r-rahmani r-rahim. In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. One hundred fourteen surahs. Count the doors as you go, and you'll find the line over all of them but one. And you'll find it once more, in a place you wouldn't expect.

The bismillah heads one hundred thirteen surahs. Surah nine, at-Tawbah, has none, and scholars give more than one reason. A report in at-Tirmidhi has the caliph 'Uthman saying it was unclear whether at-Tawbah was its own surah or the continuation of al-Anfal before it, so no line was placed between. Others said a surah opening with a stern declaration doesn't start with that line. Then the unexpected place. In surah twenty-seven, the Queen of Sheba opens a letter from Sulayman, and it begins: in the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. So the line still appears one hundred fourteen times. Not one is lost. Now look inside the line. After Allah, the first two names are ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim, both from the root r-h-m. And rahim, with a slightly different vowel, is the word for a womb. A hadith qudsi in Abu Dawud has Allah saying: I am ar-Rahman; I created the womb and gave it a name from My name. Mercy, in Arabic, sounds like where everyone began. Another hadith, in al-Bukhari and Muslim, says Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent one part to earth. From that one part, creatures are kind to each other, so that a mare lifts her hoof away from her foal. Ninety-nine are kept for the Day. And surah seven: "My mercy embraceth all things." Whatever comes after, warnings, laws, stories, the reader walks in under mercy.
screen: `113 DOORS, AND ONE IN A LETTER.`

segments.voice: If there's a Qur'an near you, turn a few pages just to see the line at the head of each surah. If not, count the doors you walked through today, waking, eating, leaving the house, opening a message, and how many could have started with that line. Then, if you'd like, say it quietly now, ahead of the next one.
Bismillah. The line that opens all but one surah, appears inside a letter in surah twenty-seven, and puts the Merciful right after Allah. Today's word.
Your line: mercy first. Every door but one opens with it. Day six hundred seventy-eight, done.

howItsDone: Muslims recite the bismillah at the start of each surah (except at-Tawbah) and before everyday actions like eating, traveling or starting work, so ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim are names of Allah said many times a day.

trapdoor: what you thought: the bismillah is a standard heading.

chat.says: Why does almost every surah start with the same line?
options: It opens every door with mercy: the Merciful, the Compassionate.
It marks the surahs revealed in Mecca rather than Medina.
It's a scribe's heading, added much later, with no meaning.
chat.meaning: The bismillah heads 113 surahs and names Allah the Merciful, the Compassionate: whatever follows, the reader walks in under mercy.

at-Tawbah.meaning: Repentance, surah nine, the one with no bismillah

'Uthman.meaning: the caliph in at-Tirmidhi's report on at-Tawbah

hadith qudsi.meaning: a hadith in which the Prophet reports Allah's words
